# Evidence Dossier for Daily Digest Issue 098 (2026-11-17)

**Search Window Used**: Past 7 days (expanded from 24 hours to ensure high-density signals across all five entrances).

### Candidate 1: Feminist Structure Signal

* **Title**: *Locating Girlhood: Place and Identity in Early American “Schoolgirl” Art*
* **Source URL**: `https://folkartmuseum.org/exhibitions/locating-girlhood-place-and-identity-in-early-american-schoolgirl-art/`
* **Publication / Event Date**: October 9, 2026 – February 28, 2027 (Special public symposiums and workshops throughout November 2026)
* **Institution / Origin**: American Folk Art Museum, New York
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Curated by Emelie Gevalt (Deputy Director and Chief Curatorial Officer) and Caroline Culp (Warren Family Assistant Curator).
  * Brings together nearly 100 needlework samplers, embroidered pictures, watercolors, and maps created by American girls and young women in the 18th and 19th centuries.
  * Reframes the genre of "schoolgirl art" through spatial identity, geography, and place, demonstrating that young female makers actively constructed landscape visuality and cartography long before the Hudson River School.
  * Expands traditional folk art history by integrating works by Black and Native American female students alongside white students.
  * Features loans from over 25 North American institutions, including The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Colonial Williamsburg, and Winterthur Museum.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Directly intersects with feminist visual culture, institutional critique, gendered labor, and spatial/landscape history. It recovers an unexamined visual archive created by young women outside academic painterly institutions.
* **Proposed Section**: Feminist Structure Signal
* **Duplication Assessment**: New candidate. The American Folk Art Museum and this exhibition have not appeared in recent issues.

### Candidate 2: Visual Culture Signal

* **Title**: *Photographic Memory: Fifty Years of Collecting*
* **Source URL**: `https://npg.si.edu/exhibition/photographic-memory-fifty-years-collecting`
* **Publication / Event Date**: November 14, 2026 – November 7, 2027
* **Institution / Origin**: National Portrait Gallery, Smithsonian Institution, Washington, D.C.
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Curated by Ann Shumard, Senior Curator of Photographs.
  * Commemorates the 50th anniversary of Congress expanding the Portrait Gallery’s mandate in 1976 to collect photography (which was previously restricted to oil paintings and sculpture).
  * Photography now accounts for nearly half of the museum's total holdings (over 11,000 objects).
  * Features over 120 historic and contemporary photographic portraits, from 1843 daguerreotypes to modern digital works.
  * Highlights include John Plumbe Jr.'s 1846 daguerreotype of Dolley Madison (paired with an 1843 daguerreotype of John Quincy Adams), Alexander Gardner's 1865 "cracked-plate" portrait of Abraham Lincoln, Sallie E. Garrity's cabinet-card of Ida B. Wells-Barnett, Lee Miller by Man Ray, W. E. B. Du Bois by Addison N. Scurlock, Roy DeCarava's Mahalia Jackson, Diane Arbus's James Brown, and Tseng Kwong Chi.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Addresses image history, media archaeology, institutional collection policy, and the democratization of visual archives through camera media.
* **Proposed Section**: Visual Culture Signal
* **Duplication Assessment**: New candidate. NPG's 50th-anniversary photography exhibition has not appeared in recent issues. (Distinguished from Paris Photo coverage in issues 11-13 and 11-14).

### Candidate 3: China / East Asia Signal

* **Title**: 2026 Seo SeMA New Media Emerging Artist Exhibition 《The Snake That Cannot Shed》 (2026 서서울미술관 뉴미디어 신진작가전 《탈피하지 못하는 뱀은》)
* **Source URL**: `https://sema.seoul.go.kr/en/whatson/exhibition/detail?exNo=1607593`
* **Publication / Event Date**: November 5, 2026 – February 28, 2027 (Press announcement Nov 10 / Nov 17, 2026)
* **Institution / Origin**: Seo-Seoul Museum of Art (SeMA), Seoul Museum of Art
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Inaugural edition of Seo SeMA's New Media Emerging Artist series, dedicated to new media experimentation.
  * Features Korean artist Okyoung Noh (노옥경, b. 1997) and Hong Kong artist Serene Hui (許思樂, b. 1992).
  * Structured around a cross-regional "pen-pal correspondence" methodology (exchanging letters, voice recordings, and research notes) instead of a shared physical studio residency.
  * Presents 6 newly commissioned works spanning video, multi-channel sound, outdoor ceramics, stone walls, and prints, exhibited alongside records of their correspondence.
  * Investigates ancestral silences, family trauma, and migration histories across South Korea and Hong Kong, taking Nietzsche's aphorism on skin-shedding (*"The snake which cannot cast its skin has to perish"*) as a conceptual framework for bodily and structural transformation.
* **Relevance to Muki**: High-density East Asian visual signal combining feminist/queer correspondence methods, family archives, trauma memory, and multi-sensory new media installation.
* **Proposed Section**: China / East Asia Signal
* **Duplication Assessment**: New candidate. Neither artist nor Seo SeMA has appeared in recent issues.

### Candidate 4: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal

* **Title**: *HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents*
* **Source URL**: `https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06013`
* **Publication Date**: November 9, 2026
* **Authors / Origin**: Haozhen Zhang, Bohan Liu, Jianzhu Bao, Qingyuan Liu, Haodong Yue, Xiao Li, Zi Pong Lim, Wenya Wang (arXiv:2611.06013)
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Proposes *HiVe-Mem*, a 2D memory framework designed for multimodal AI agents operating in long-horizon interaction histories.
  * Combines "Horizontal Memory Expansion" (organizing memory episodes into a relational graph using visual and text anchors) and "Vertical Evidence Composition" (retaining multi-layered evidence per episode, including summaries, captions, visual crops, raw images, and raw interaction logs).
  * Employs a lightweight trainable selector to dynamically compose query-adaptive evidence subsets.
  * Reduces agent token consumption by ~90% while consistently improving task accuracy across three multimodal memory benchmarks.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Directly addresses AI-native creative and research workflows, context retention in multimodal agent systems, visual memory architecture, and knowledge management without context token explosion.
* **Proposed Section**: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal
* **Duplication Assessment**: New candidate. Differs from previous agent frameworks (AgiWorld in 11-16, Reviso in 11-15, VideoMaker in 11-14, Video-Coder in 11-13, WikiTrace in 11-12, Cassette-Editor in 11-09) by focusing specifically on 2D relational-graph visual evidence composition for long-horizon multimodal agents.

### Candidate 5: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity

* **Title**: Open Call for Inlaks–AAA Art Grant 2027
* **Source URL**: `https://aaa.org.hk/en/collection/search/library/open-call-for-inlaks-aaa-art-grant-2027`
* **Publication Date / Deadline**: Launched November 5, 2026; Deadline November 30, 2026
* **Institution / Origin**: Asia Art Archive (AAA) in India & Inlaks India Foundation
* **Verified Facts**:
  * Dedicated to supporting experimental art practice that uses research, collaboration, workshops, and formal experimentation to interrogate the archive.
  * Invites proposals engaging with personal archives (letters, scrapbooks, photo albums), public libraries, databases, maps, and inventories across art, cinema, theatre, law, or science.
  * Open to Indian visual artists and collectives aged 25 to 35 residing in India.
  * Provides grant funding up to INR 2,00,000 for projects running from January 1 to December 31, 2027.
* **Relevance to Muki**: High-quality research grant focusing explicitly on the archive as a system, medium, and counter-historical tool within East Asian/South Asian contexts.
* **Proposed Section**: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity
* **Duplication Assessment**: New candidate. While Asia Art Archive appeared in 11-15 for the Ming Fay Fellowship (NYU A/P/A), this is a separate, newly opened research grant for artists using the archive as medium (Inlaks–AAA Art Grant 2027).
